<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Implement an unsigned 8bit multiplier based on pipelining processing.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal that controls the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="MUL_WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="MUL_OUT_WIDTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_en_out_reg">
            <description>mul_en_out_reg is a 3-bit register that stores the input enable signal mul_en_in. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 when rst_n is 0. The register is used to control the output enable signal mul_en_out.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <reset_event>rst_n == 0</reset_event>
            <update_expression>mul_en_out_reg <= {mul_en_out_reg[1:0], mul_en_in}</update_expression>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="mul_en_out">
            <description>mul_en_out is a combinational logic that outputs the most significant bit of mul_en_out_reg. It is used to indicate if the multiplication operation is enabled.</description>
            <output_expression>mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg[2]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_a_reg">
            <description>mul_a_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input multiplicand signal mul_a. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 when rst_n is 0. The register is used to store the multiplicand value.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <reset_event>rst_n == 0</reset_event>
            <update_expression>mul_a_reg <= mul_en_in ? mul_a : mul_a_reg</update_expression>
        </sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_b_reg">
            <description>mul_b_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input multiplier signal mul_b. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 when rst_n is 0. The register is used to store the multiplier value.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <reset_event>rst_n == 0</reset_event>
            <update_expression>mul_b_reg <= mul_en_in ? mul_b : mul_b_reg</update_expression>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[0]">
            <description>temp[0] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the least significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[0] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[0]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[1]">
            <description>temp[1] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the second least significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[1] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[1]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[2]">
            <description>temp[2] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the third least significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[2] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[2]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[3]">
            <description>temp[3] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the fourth least significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[3] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[3]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[4]">
            <description>temp[4] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the fifth least significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[4] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[4]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[5]">
            <description>temp[5] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the sixth least significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[5] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[5]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[6]">
            <description>temp[6] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the seventh least significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[6] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[6]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp[7]">
            <description>temp[7] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the least significant bit of mul_a_reg and the most significant bit of mul_b_reg. It is used to store the partial product value.</description>
            <output_expression>temp[7] = mul_a_reg[0] & mul_b_reg[7]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum[0]">
            <description>sum[0] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial sum generated by the addition of temp[0] and temp[1]. It is used to store the partial sum value.</description>
            <output_expression>sum[0] = temp[0] + temp[1]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum[1]">
            <description>sum[1] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial sum generated by the addition of temp[2] and temp[3]. It is used to store the partial sum value.</description>
            <output_expression>sum[1] = temp[2] + temp[3]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum[2]">
            <description>sum[2] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial sum generated by the addition of temp[4] and temp[5]. It is used to store the partial sum value.</description>
            <output_expression>sum[2] = temp[4] + temp[5]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum[3]">
            <description>sum[3] is a 9-bit wire that stores the partial sum generated by the addition of temp[6] and temp[7]. It is used to store the partial sum value.</description>
            <output_expression>sum[3] = temp[6] + temp[7]</output_expression>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum[4]">
            <description>sum[4] is a 10-bit wire that stores the partial sum generated by the addition of sum[0] and sum[1]. It is used to store the partial sum value.</description>
            <output_expression>sum[4] = sum[0] + sum[1]</output_expression>
